'''Andrei Vladlenovich Zelevinsky''' ({{lang|ru|Андрей Владленович Зелевинский}}; 30 January 1953 – 10 April 2013)<ref>[https://www.commalg.org/ News on website for the commutative algebra community]</ref> was a Russian-American mathematician who made important contributions to [[algebra]], [[combinatorics]], and [[representation theory]], among other areas.

==Biography==
Zelevinsky graduated in 1969 from the [[:ru:Лицей "Вторая школа"|Moscow Mathematical School No. 2]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sch2.ru/content/view/46/61/ |title=Medal-winning graduates of the Moscow Mathematical School No. 2 |access-date=2013-04-18 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130615191604/http://sch2.ru/content/view/46/61/ |archive-date=2013-06-15 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
After winning a silver medal as a member of the USSR team at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]<ref>[https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=10170 IMO Results]</ref> he was admitted without examination to the mathematics department of [[Moscow State University]]
where he obtained his PhD in 1978 under the mentorship of [[Joseph Bernstein]],
[[Alexandre Kirillov]] and [[Israel Gelfand]].<ref>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=42004 A. Zelevinsky at the Mathematics Genealogy Project].</ref>

He worked<ref>[http://www.math.neu.edu/zelevinsky/mycv.html A. Zelevinsky's cv] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130416191132/http://www.math.neu.edu/zelevinsky/mycv.html |date=April 16, 2013 }}</ref> in the mathematical laboratory of [[Vladimir Keilis-Borok]] at the [[:ru:Институт физики Земли имени О. Ю. Шмидта РАН|Institute of Earth Science]] (1977–85), and at the Council for Cybernetics of the Soviet Academy of Sciences (1985–90). In the early 1980s, at a great personal risk, he taught at the [[Jewish People's University]],<ref>[http://www.ftpi.umn.edu/shifman/ComradeEinstein.pdf You failed your math test, comrade Einstein]</ref> an unofficial organization offering first-class mathematics education to talented students denied admission to Moscow State University's math department.

In 1990–91, Zelevinsky was a visiting professor at [[Cornell University]], and from 1991 until his death was on faculty at [[Northeastern University]], Boston.
With his wife, Galina, he had a son and a daughter; he also had several grandchildren.<ref>[http://www.math.neu.edu/news/andrei-zelevinsky-1953-2013/11_april_13 Northeastern University, Math. Dep page] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501023619/http://www.math.neu.edu/news/andrei-zelevinsky-1953-2013/11_april_13 |date=May 1, 2013 }}</ref>

Zelevinsky is a relative of the physicists [[Vladimir Zelevinsky]] and [[Tanya Zelevinsky]].

==Research==
Zelevinsky's most notable achievement is the discovery (with [[Sergey Fomin]]) of [[cluster algebra]]s.
His other contributions include:

* [[Bernstein–Zelevinsky classification]] of representations of [[p-adic group|''p''-adic groups]];
* Introduction (jointly with [[Israel Gelfand]] and [[Mikhail Kapranov]]) of A-systems of hypergeometric equations (also known as GKZ-systems)<ref>Israel M. Gelfand, Mikhail M. Kapranov, Andrei V. Zelevinsky, Hypergeometric functions and toric varieties, (Russian) Funktsional. Anal. i Prilozhen. 23 (1989), no. 2, 12–26; translation in Funct. Anal. Appl. 23 (1989), no. 2, 94–10</ref> and development of the theory of [[hyperdeterminant]]s;<ref>
{{cite book
 | last       = Gelfand | first      = Israel M.  | author2 =  Mikhail M. Kapranov |author3=Andrei V. Zelevinsky
 | title      = Discriminants, resultants, and multidimensional determinants
 | publisher  = Boston: Birkhäuser | year       = 1994
 | isbn       = 0-8176-3660-9
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Roberts|first=David P.|date=2009|title=Review: Discriminants, Resultants, and Multidimensional Determinants, by I. M. Gelfand, M. M. Kapranov, and A. V. Zelevinsky|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/discriminants-resultants-and-multidimensional-determinants|access-date=1 Jul 2020|website=Mathematical Association of America}}</ref>
* generalization of the [[Littlewood–Richardson rule]] and [[Robinson–Schensted correspondence]] using the combinatorics of [[Picture (mathematics)|"pictures"]];
* work (jointly with [[Arkady Berenstein]] and [[Sergey Fomin]]) on [[Totally positive matrix|total positivity]];
* work (with Sergey Fomin) on the [[Pierre Alphonse Laurent|Laurent]] phenomenon, including its applications to [[Somos sequence]]s.

* [[Humboldt Prize|Humboldt Research Award (2004)]]<!--<ref>[http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_hn_query.humboldtianer_details?p_externe_id=7000181492&p_lang=en Humboldt Research Award]</ref>
[http://www.northeastern.edu/academichonors/faculty/university-distinguished-professors/index.html Northeastern University, Academic Honors Convocation],</ref><ref>[http://www.avh.de/web/humboldt-award.html Humboldt Research Award]</ref>-->
* Fellow (2012) of the American Mathematical Society<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>
* University Distinguished Professorship (2013) at Northeastern University<ref>[https://www.northeastern.edu/academichonors/faculty/university-distinguished-professors/award-recipients.html Northeastern University, Academic Honors Convocation]</ref><!-- [http://www.math.neu.edu/news/andrei-zelevinsky-1953-2013/11_april_13 Northeastern University, Math. Dep page]</ref>-->
* [[Leroy P. Steele Prize|Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research (2018)]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=3803 2018 Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research in Discrete Mathematics/Logic to Sergey Fomin and Andrei Zelevinsky]</ref>
